name: diya-submit
description: Keep your bookkeeping in DIY Accounting Submit from your assistant: read and change your DIYA-GL books, work out a UK VAT return under Making Tax Digital (MTD), company accounts and a Company Tax Return from your records, then open the link the assistant gives you and check and file each one yourself on the Submit site.

interface.longDescription:
Keep your bookkeeping in DIY Accounting Submit and work out what you file from your records, from your assistant.

What it does:
- Lists the DIYA-GL books saved in your account and opens one. A DIYA-GL book is one business's sales, purchases and bank lines for a year.
- Reads your records: the profit and loss account, balance sheet, tax and VAT figures, the book checks, your largest customers and suppliers, and the chart of accounts.
- Records or corrects sales, purchases and bank lines, saving each change as a new version of the DIYA-GL book, with an undo. Starts a new DIYA-GL book, next year's, or a company's next year from the Companies House register.
- Derives the nine boxes of an MTD VAT return for a quarter, with the lines behind them, and a company's micro-entity or small company accounts and Company Tax Return.
- Gives you a link to the VAT, accounts or Company Tax Return form on the Submit site with the figures filled in. You open it, check the figures and file it yourself in the browser.
- Looks up a tax rule, rate or deadline with the gov.uk page that states it, and a company's filing deadlines on the Companies House register.
- Reads the receipts stored for the VAT returns and accounts you filed.

Who it is for: a UK business that keeps its records in DIY Accounting Submit, for example a limited company (Ltd) or a sole trader.

Limits: no tool in this plugin files a return or accounts, or pays HMRC. You need an existing DIY Accounting Submit account. The plugin gives no tax advice.
capabilities: Keep your bookkeeping in DIYA-GL books saved in your DIY Accounting Submit account
Read the profit and loss account, balance sheet and book checks of a DIYA-GL book
Find your largest customers, suppliers and costs in your records
Record or correct sales, purchases and bank lines, with an undo
Start a new DIYA-GL book, next year's, or a company's from the Companies House register
Work out a Making Tax Digital (MTD) VAT return from your records
Work out a company's micro-entity or small company accounts and Company Tax Return
Give a link to file the VAT return, accounts or Company Tax Return in the browser
Look up a tax rule, rate or deadline with its gov.uk source
Read your stored VAT and accounts receipts
defaultPrompt: Work out my MTD VAT return for the quarter ended 30 June 2025
Who were my five biggest customers last year?
Prepare my company's accounts to file at Companies House

publication.release_notes: Version 0.1.8. The plugin now keeps your bookkeeping as well as working out your VAT: it reads the figures, lines and checks of your DIYA-GL books, records and corrects lines with an undo, starts new DIYA-GL books, works out company accounts and a Company Tax Return, gives links that open the VAT, accounts and Company Tax Return forms with the figures filled in, and looks up tax rules and rates with their gov.uk sources. The listing says DIYA-GL book and your records.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. A person signs in to an existing DIY Accounting Submit account and uses what that account already has.

positive.description: Work out an MTD VAT return for a quarter
positive.prompt: Work out my MTD VAT return for the quarter ended 30 June 2025.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant asks which book or opens BrickWork Pro Ltd, then shows the nine VAT boxes for the quarter ended 30 June 2025 with their amounts and points out lines in the quarter worth checking before filing.

positive.description: Show the lines behind box 1 and box 4
positive.prompt: Which lines are behind box 1 and box 4 of my VAT return?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant names the largest sales lines behind box 1 and the largest purchase lines behind box 4, each with its date, description and VAT amount.

positive.prompt: Give me the link to file it.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant gives a link to the VAT form on the Submit site with the figures filled in, and says the person checks and files in the browser.

positive.description: Get the link to file company accounts
positive.prompt: Prepare my company's accounts to file at Companies House.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant gives a link to the micro-entity accounts form on the Submit site with the figures filled in, and says the person looks up the company, checks the figures and files in the browser, and that nothing has been filed.

positive.description: Find the largest customers in the records
positive.prompt: Who were my five biggest customers last year?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant opens BrickWork Pro Ltd and names its largest customers by total sales in the DIYA-GL book, with each total.

negative.description: No tool in the plugin files a return. The assistant does not file it: it offers the link from prepare_vat_return, says the person ticks the declaration and files in the browser, and says nothing has been filed.
negative.prompt: File my VAT return for me.

negative.description: No tool in the plugin pays HMRC or anyone else. The assistant says it cannot pay. It says the person pays HMRC through their own bank or HMRC's service.

No tool in the plugin files accounts. The assistant does not file them: it offers the link from prepare_micro_entity_accounts or prepare_small_company_accounts, says the person files in the browser, and says nothing has been filed.
negative.prompt: File my company accounts for me.
